definitions.gloss: occasionally, from time to time, now and then
definitions.explanation: Indicates that something happens at irregular intervals, not frequently but not rarely either. Slightly more literary than ときどき.

examples.japanese: {時折|ときおり}{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}る。
examples.english: It rains from time to time.

examples.japanese: {時折|ときおり}{昔|むかし}のことを{思|おも}い{出|だ}す。
examples.english: I occasionally recall things from the past.

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}の{外|そと}では、{時折|ときおり}{強|つよ}い{風|かぜ}が{木々|きぎ}を{揺|ゆ}らしていた。
examples.english: Outside the window, a strong wind was shaking the trees from time to time.

notes:
{時折|ときおり} is a slightly literary synonym of {時々|ときどき}. It is preferred in written Japanese and formal narration.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {時折|ときおり} + verb: occasionally ~
- {時折|ときおり}{見|み}せる〜: ~ that one shows from time to time

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {時々|ときどき}: sometimes (most common, casual and neutral)
- {時折|ときおり}: occasionally (slightly literary)
- たまに: once in a while (casual, lower frequency)
- {折|おり}に{触|ふ}れて: on occasion (formal)

USAGE: {時折|ときおり} suggests a somewhat irregular, unpredictable pattern. It often appears in descriptive writing, conveying an atmospheric quality.
